newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-BOARDMAN STARTS TOUR ON A HIGH NOTE.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-BOARDMAN STARTS TOUR ON A HIGH NOTE.

text.p: Chris Boardman erased painful memories when he took the Tour de France leader's yellow jersey with a brilliant victory in the prologue on Saturday.

Three years after winning his first Tour prologue, the Briton once again confirmed he was the world's best time trial specialist with a ride of eight minutes 20.90 seconds on a flat 7.3-km course in the streets of Rouen in the north of France.
Boardman's win, at an average speed of 52.466 kph, was all the more convincing as his nearest rival in this year's prologue, German Jan Ullrich, started two hours before him in far better conditions.
Ullrich, second in the 1996 Tour behind Denmark's Bjarne Riis, was two seconds slower than the GAN rider with Russia's Yevgeny Berzin third, five seconds behind Boardman.
For the Briton, who has now won 30 prologues, this was his race of the season, especially after the disappointment of his two previous Tour prologues.
In 1995, he crashed out of the race in the rain and he was beaten last year by just two seconds by Swiss Alex Zuelle.
"For me this was the hardest day of the year because I did not know whether good or bad would come out of it. It's a lot of pressure but it is good pressure," Boardman said.
The world one hour record holder added the win was even more special as he had not fully realised what the yellow jersey meant to a professional rider when he first took it in Lille in 1994.
There was also another important personal challenge for the 28-year-old from Manchester.
"When you receive the yellow jersey, they also give you a toy lion. My second son, Oscar, did not have his," he said.

Ullrich confirmed he may well be the main threat to his Telekom team leader Riis following Saturday's second placing. The 23-year-old German, who won the last time trial of the 1996 Tour, is obviously in great shape.
Riis had to be content with 13th place. But the 33-year-old Dane has never been at his best in prologues and he has three weeks and more than 3,900 kms ahead of him to claim his jersey back.
Spain's Abraham Olano also had an average ride, finishing eighth, 11 seconds behind Boardman.
Despite entering the Tour with a broken collarbone, Zuelle showed he could not be ruled out, finishing fifth in the same time as Berzin and veteran compatriot Tony Rominger.
Sunday's first stage takes the 198 tour riders from Forges-les-Eaux to Rouen over 192 kms and should favour sprinters.
